standard_prerequisites: The three functors attached to a map of quasi-coherent modules, and the scheme theoretic support of a finite type module with its quasi-compactness over the base
Etale localization of surjectivity and of injectivity of maps of quasi-coherent modules, and the behaviour of scheme theoretic supports under base change
The algebra lemma describing when a surjective, injective or bijective map of modules over a directed limit of rings already has the property at a finite stage
Finiteness of the kernel of a surjection of a finite type module onto a finitely presented module, and containment of its support in that of the source
core_obligations: Part one: replace the space by the scheme theoretic support of the target and the map by its restriction, so that the morphism becomes quasi-compact; then, over a directed limit of affine base schemes, localise along a surjective etale morphism from an affine scheme that is itself a directed limit, and invoke the algebra criterion for surjectivity

Part two: keep track of the quasi-compact scheme theoretic support of the source, choose an affine etale chart whose image contains the special fibre support, and invoke the algebra criterion for injectivity, again using that the charts form a directed limit

Part three: first apply part one to obtain surjectivity at some stage, then form the kernel of the map at that stage and note that it is of finite type with support contained in the quasi-compact support of the source, so that part two applies to the kernel map and produces a stage where it vanishes, which is exactly a stage where the original map is an isomorphism
proof_roadmap: Reduce part one to the quasi-compact case and localise along affine etale charts to apply the algebra criterion for surjectivity
Do the same for injectivity in part two, controlling the quasi-compact support
In part three get surjectivity at a stage, then kill the kernel of finite type by part two
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the limit preservation of the three functors of surjectivity, vanishing and isomorphism at source lines 1334-1349, label lemma-iso-limits, whose proof occupies source lines 1351-1417. The proof is a three part limit argument of substance: part one reduces to the quasi-compact case by passing to the scheme theoretic support and then localises along a surjective etale morphism from an affine scheme which is itself a directed limit, so that an algebra criterion for surjectivity applies; part two does the same for injectivity while controlling the quasi-compact scheme theoretic support of the source through an affine etale chart; and part three is a nontrivial combination, obtaining surjectivity at some stage, forming the kernel, proving that kernel is of finite type with support inside a quasi-compact one, and applying part two to it. The counted statement records neither the reductions nor the kernel argument.
